QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_49

question.text: The Investment Manager of a Category III AIF may have incentive to take riskier or more speculative positions because:

answer.text: Higher incentive fees are earned on higher returns, tempting speculative bets
Hurdle rate falls automatically with risk
GST is exempt on speculative trades

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Ch 9.5 Point 2: 'Incentive Fee' risk — IM may choose riskier investments to earn higher incentive fees, in contrast to Cat III's stated objectives. Classic principal-agent problem. **The Trap:** Option A is false — mgmt fees are on GNAV, not volatility. Options C and D are invented. **Cross-Exam Context:** X-A/B (Investment Adviser) covers IM conflicts; XIX-B tests this for Cat III. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Mitigation: tie part of GP commitment (skin-in-the-game) to back-end carry with clawback. SEBI now requires minimum GP continuing interest — document it clearly in the PPM.
